title: Onboard flame during Saturn V first-stage cutoff
summary: A sealed methane/air chamber aboard the Saturn V. The window spans S-IC engine cutoff and S-II ignition: sensed acceleration drops from about 4.8 g to under 1 g (the legacy model ignites the second stage at separation, so there is no free-fall gap), and that history drives buoyancy in the chamber.
expected_behaviour: Before cutoff the plume is strongly accelerated along the thrust axis; after staging the buoyant driving is several times weaker.
acceptance_checks: Coupled run completes and both streams share one experiment ID.
Applied axial acceleration magnitude before cutoff exceeds 40 m/s2 and after staging is below 12 m/s2.
The S-IC cutoff event is listed inside the window with its flight and chamber times.
